The exam

ExamAAMI / ACI Certified Biomedical Equipment Technician
CodeCBET
QuestionsUp to 165
Time180 minutes
PassingThe real exam requires about 116 of 165 correct, roughly 70%. This course's official-format test uses 70%.
Lessons60 lessons across 9 units, about 10.5 hours of reading

Exam domains

DomainWeightLessons
Anatomy and Physiology7%7

How the course works

  1. Cheat sheet. Everything the exam expects you to recall cold, printable.
  2. Starter test. A few questions per exam domain, with a confidence rating on each.
  3. Your tutorial. Lessons chosen from what you missed or guessed, each with a checkpoint and a deeper explanation.
  4. Practice tests and retraining. 50 questions, weighted like the real exam. Every miss is explained and feeds back into your lessons.
  5. 3 of your last 5 at 80%. That unlocks one full-length test on the real exam's clock: 165 questions in 180 minutes, at its real passing score of 70%. Pass it once and you are ready to book.

Every lesson

The first 15 lessons are open to read here. Every lesson, with its checkpoint, is free inside the course.

Unit 1: Anatomy and Physiology

The body systems a biomed's equipment monitors, supports, and replaces, and the vocabulary clinicians use to describe them.

  1. Body Organization, Terminology, and the Skin 8 min
  2. The Cardiovascular System 11 min
  3. The Respiratory System 9 min
  4. The Nervous and Musculoskeletal Systems 9 min
  5. Gastrointestinal, Endocrine, Renal, and Blood 8 min
  6. Skin, Skeleton, Muscle, and the Brain in Detail 10 min
  7. Digestion, Lymph and Immunity, Hormones, Kidneys, Reproduction, and Blood Terms 11 min

Unit 2: Fundamentals of Electricity and Electronics

The theory behind every circuit you troubleshoot, and the power systems that keep a hospital running.

  1. Voltage, Current, Resistance, and Power 10 min
  2. AC, Transformers, Hospital Power Distribution, and Isolation 11 min
  3. Passive Components, Filters, and Reading Schematics 10 min
  4. Active Devices, Power Supplies, and Amplifiers 10 min
  5. Batteries, UPS, and Power Conditioning 9 min
  6. Circuit Analysis: Energy, Dividers, Kirchhoff's Laws, Bridges, and Op-Amp Gain 11 min
  7. AC Power, Impedance, Transducers, Batteries by the Numbers, and Regulators 11 min

On exam day

  • 165 questions in 3 hours, closed book, with a simple calculator allowed. That is over a minute per question; do not rush the math items.
  • Some questions are unscored trial items. A question that seems to be from nowhere may be one of them; answer it and move on.
  • Read for the qualifier: FIRST, MOST likely, BEST. In problem-solving items the first step is usually the patient, then the simplest cause, then the accessory.
  • Know the safety numbers cold: leakage limits and the current thresholds, ECG paper math, pressure and temperature conversions, and the infusion rate formula.
  • Two forms of ID, arrive early, sleep the night before.
